## Design

### What we drew

Session replays showed people abandoning at identity verification, not at the
form itself — they were waiting, not confused. That reframed the work: the
problem was perceived duration, not layout. We redrew the flow so verification
runs in the background while the user keeps moving, and designed the states
nobody had specced — the slow case, the retry, the hard failure.

## Build

### What we shipped

The same three people who drew it built it, so nothing was lost explaining it.
Onboarding became a server-driven sequence: the client renders whatever steps
the API describes, which means copy and ordering change without an app release.
Verification moved to a background queue so the interface never blocks on it.

<div class="placeholder" style="height: 440px">Architecture — services, queue, and the verification path</div>

## Outcome

Signup abandonment fell 38% over the first 90 days, and median time to first
transaction dropped from just over four minutes to a little under one. The
design system went to Northwind's own team, who have since shipped two
surfaces on it without us.

We stayed on retainer for the following quarter to cover the payments work.
